name: What is included in preconstruction for a luxury remodel or custom home?

mainEntity.name: What services should be included in preconstruction before construction starts?
mainEntity.text: What services should be included in preconstruction before construction starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Preconstruction should do more than produce a rough estimate. For a luxury remodel or custom home, it should clarify what the site can support, what the city is likely to require, and what the project will probably cost and take to build. Common services include zoning and feasibility review, preliminary design coordination, budgeting, scheduling, permit path planning, consultant management, and constructability review. A stronger preconstruction package may also include a survey, geotechnical review, utility coordination, structural input, preliminary selection of materials, and a list of long-lead items that could affect timing. The purpose is to reduce unknowns before the project is committed to full design and permitting. Ask for a written scope of preconstruction so you can see exactly what the firm is responsible for and what is excluded. Some firms only provide estimating and basic planning, while others manage the entire early-phase process. For homeowners in Los Angeles, that difference matters because hillside conditions, neighborhood constraints, and local permitting can add complexity quickly. The best preconstruction phase creates a clear path from concept to permit-ready plans with fewer change orders and fewer budget surprises.
acceptedAnswer.description: Preconstruction usually includes site review, feasibility checks, design coordination, budget estimating, permit strategy, consultant coordination, schedule planning, and value engineering. For custom homes and major remodels, it may also include structural review, survey work, geotechnical input, utility research, and long-lead item planning. The exact scope should be written clearly so you know what is included before you sign.
